cohort: 371 women (193 spontaneous vaginal deliveries and 178 cesarean deliveries) at a women's health hospital in Turkey.
finding: The study found a lack of adherence to evidence-based practices during labor and delivery, suggesting a need for improved implementation of these practices in hospital settings.
mod_finding: Skin-to-skin contact was not provided to any mothers or newborns in both spontaneous and cesarean delivery groups, 73.1% of the spontaneous birth group underwent labor induction, none of the women in labor had a support person (other than medical staff), and upright birthing positions were not used during delivery in the spontaneous birth group.
